title: the-tin-rocket
characterStill: SUBJECT: a man in his early forties, lean and long-limbed, photographed centered in frame, three-quarter view, mid-motion as he checks a strap at his own chest, eyes down on his hands, never toward the lens. FACE (face-lock, invariant anchors): a 2cm pale scar splitting the outer end of the right eyebrow, the hairs growing crooked around it; a nose broken once, the ridge bent slightly toward the left with a faint shine of old scar tissue on the bridge; hazel eyes, pale sun-creases fanning from the outer corners, lower lids faintly puffed from thin sleep; three-day stubble flecked grey with a sharp beard edge along the jawline and one bare patch under the left corner of the mouth; dark brown hair cropped short, a stubborn cowlick standing at the crown, grey starting at both temples; a single vertical worry line between the brows. HANDS: broad palms, knuckles chapped and slightly swollen, a callus ridge across both palms under the fingers, right thumbnail bruised dark at its base, nails clipped blunt, thin grease lines in the cuticles. WARDROBE: he wears all of — a chalk-white pressure suit of stiff ribbed fabric yellowed faintly at the elbows, its long front zip closed to the sternum with a fabric pull tab frayed at the end; a soft grey inner collar ring scuffed grey-brown where a helmet has seated hundreds of times; a shoulder patch of a plain navy circle stitched with slightly loose thread at its lower edge; twin metal cuff rings at the wrists, one scratched bright; suit legs creased permanently at the knee from sitting; thin white glove liners pushed down and bunched at the wrists. GEAR: a five-point harness of pale webbing across his chest, each strap fed through a black adjuster buckle, the central metal latch plate rubbed to bare steel at its corners; a narrow oxygen umbilical of grey corrugated hose clipped at his left hip by a spring hook with paint worn off the gate; a short braided lanyard hanging from a D-ring at his right hip, its free clip empty and swinging. LIGHT: hard motivated key from a caged overhead work lamp above and slightly behind him, a warm amber fill from a sodium bulb off frame-left, a cold cyan spill from an instrument panel low on his chest. PALETTE + GRAIN: sodium amber highlights against deep cyan-teal shadows, desaturated whites, shallow depth of field with the background falling to soft bokeh, fine 35mm film grain, gentle halation on the brightest edges. Photorealistic. No text, no watermark, no border.
setStill: CENTERPIECE: a homemade reflecting telescope standing in a cramped garage loft, part by part — a cardboard main tube 90cm long wrapped in oxblood electrical tape whose overlapping seams have lifted at three places; a brass focuser barrel at the top, its knurled knob polished bright by fingers on one side only and green-dulled on the other; a plywood mirror cell at the base, held by three brass thumbscrews, one replaced with a longer mismatched screw; a counterweight of stacked steel washers bound to the tube with wire, sagging slightly; a pipe tripod of galvanised plumbing elbows, one leg shimmed with a folded matchbook on the uneven planks. SURFACES: bare pine floor planks, dark and glossy along the walking line, splintered at the hatch edge; a pegboard wall with hooks and clean pale silhouettes where tools used to hang; a workbench top of scarred plywood, grey with sawdust, ringed by old mug stains and one long clean streak wiped by a sleeve; a tin rocket model on the bench, soup-can body painted matte red with a hand-brushed white stripe, three sheet-metal fins soldered slightly crooked, a dent on the nose, glue crust at the seams. LIGHT-SOURCES: a single caged work bulb hanging from a knotted brown cord, filament visible, throwing hard amber light and a shadow of its own cage across the pegboard; a sodium streetlamp far below the open roof hatch, pushing a cold-warm shaft of orange up through frost on the hatch glass; a faint cyan city glow along the rafters. WEATHER + TIME: a clear, still, cold October night, frost blooming at the corners of the hatch glass, breath-mist hanging in the bulb light, no rain. PALETTE + GRAIN: sodium amber highlights against deep cyan-teal shadows, desaturated whites, shallow depth of field with the far wall in soft bokeh, fine 35mm film grain, gentle halation on the bulb filament. Photorealistic. No text, no watermark, no border.

shots.title: the-boy-hears-it
shots.firstFrame: Low camera height, lens just above the workbench of the room from the reference image, wide-to-medium size, 16:9. The boy sits off-center to frame-right at the homemade telescope, body angled frame-left toward the eyepiece, one eye still at the focuser, breath misting in the caged bulb's amber light. The tin rocket sits in the foreground bench dust, unpainted dent catching light. In frame: the boy at the eyepiece, the homemade telescope on its pipe tripod, the tin rocket on the dusty bench, the caged work bulb lit above, the open roof hatch with frost on its glass, the pegboard wall with empty hooks.
shots.motion: Camera pushes in slowly and low from behind the bench as the boy from the reference image lifts his eye off the eyepiece and turns his head toward the open roof hatch. He hesitates, re-grips the brass focuser knob with cold-stiff fingers, then lets it go. His sleeve drags a clean streak through the dust beside the tin rocket. One continuous take. SFX: a metal focuser click, a chair leg scraping planks, one shallow indrawn breath. Ambient noise: a deep off-screen rocket rumble building far away, crickets, wind combing the roof.
shots.altCharacter: SECOND CHARACTER (same person, age nine): a small thin boy, shoulders narrow inside his clothes. FACE: hazel eyes identical to the canon man's, the same stubborn cowlick standing at the crown of dark brown hair, the right eyebrow still smooth and unmarked where the scar will one day come, a nose still straight, front teeth slightly large, a scatter of freckles across the nose bridge, dust smudged along the left cheek. HANDS: small, bitten nails, a graphite smudge on the right forefinger, knuckles pink from cold. WARDROBE: he wears all of — a navy knit sweater with a snagged pull at the right elbow and cuffs stretched loose; a striped cotton pyjama shirt collar showing above the sweater neck; corduroy trousers worn shiny at the knees, the hem turned up once; mismatched wool socks, no shoes. Lit by the caged amber work bulb above and the cold sodium shaft from the hatch.

shots.title: contrail-over-the-rooftops
shots.firstFrame: POV from inside the loft, camera at the boy's eye height looking up and out through the open roof hatch of the room from the reference image, wide size, 16:9. Frost rims the hatch glass in the near foreground; the tin rocket stands in silhouette on the hatch ledge at frame-left. Beyond, sodium-lit rooftops and a single white contrail climbing off-center to frame-right through cold cyan sky. In frame: the frosted hatch glass, the tin rocket in silhouette on the ledge, the rooftop tiles and one aerial mast, the climbing contrail, the sodium-orange skyline glow, the first stars.
shots.motion: Camera tilts up slowly through the hatch and holds, hand-held breath in the frame, as the contrail widens and drifts sideways in the high wind, its bright head shrinking toward the stars. Frost on the near glass softens and beads where warm air from the loft touches it, one drop tracking down. One continuous take. SFX: a low rolling rumble arriving late, glass ticking as it warms. Ambient noise: distant dog barking off-screen, wind over roof tiles, faint traffic hum below.

shots.title: harness-in-the-trainer
shots.firstFrame: Eye-level camera, medium-wide, 16:9, inside a cramped grey gimbal trainer cabin. The man from the reference image sits off-center to frame-right in the trainer seat, angled frame-left, hauling one harness strap across his chest, eyes down on the latch plate. Foreground frame-left: a padded strut cutting the frame. The tin rocket, red paint chipped, is wedged upright in a mesh pocket beside his knee. In frame: the man from the reference image working the harness, the trainer seat and its five-point webbing, the padded strut in foreground, the tin rocket in the mesh pocket, a caged work lamp overhead, one cyan instrument panel glowing frame-left.
shots.motion: Camera trucks slowly frame-left at eye level as the man from the reference image hauls the harness strap tight across his chest. The webbing slips through the buckle once; he shifts his shoulder, sets his cold-stiff fingers again and pulls harder, the strap biting a pale crease into the suit fabric. Sweat shines at his temple. He glances down at the tin rocket by his knee. One continuous take. SFX: webbing hissing through a metal adjuster, a latch plate clack, an exhaled grunt. Ambient noise: an off-screen intercom voice counting readiness, fans droning, hydraulic whine below the floor.

shots.title: insert-the-strap-bites
shots.firstFrame: Macro insert, camera low and close at chest height, shallow focus, 16:9. The hands of the man from the reference image fill frame-right mid-pull on the harness webbing, the steel latch plate half-seated, the strap already creasing the suit fabric. Frame-left foreground, softly out of focus, the tin rocket leans in its mesh pocket, chipped red paint catching the cyan panel light. In frame: his two hands mid-pull, the harness webbing and steel latch plate, the creased suit fabric, the tin rocket blurred in the mesh pocket, the cyan panel glow.
shots.motion: Camera holds tight and drifts a few centimetres right as his hands finish the pull already in progress. The latch plate slips out of his fingers, he re-grips with the heel of his palm and forces it home on the second try, seating it with a snap that leaves a fresh bright scratch across the plate corner. His knuckles whiten, then release. One continuous take. SFX: metal snap, fabric creak, a short breath through the teeth. Ambient noise: off-screen intercom voice calling a hold, fan drone, distant hydraulic groan.

shots.title: clipping-it-in
shots.firstFrame: High camera, angled down over the man's shoulder, medium size, 16:9, inside the launch capsule. The man from the reference image lies strapped off-center to frame-left, facing frame-left toward the console, lifting the tin rocket toward a short braided lanyard clipped at the panel ledge. Foreground top-right: a soft-focus switch guard. In frame: the man from the reference image holding the tin rocket, the braided lanyard and its spring clip on the panel ledge, the console with cyan-lit dials, the harness across his chest, the switch guard in foreground, one small window showing pale dawn.
shots.motion: Camera drifts down and slightly frame-left over his shoulder as he hooks the tin rocket's wire loop onto the lanyard clip. His gloved fingers fumble the gate once, he pauses, breathes, then seats the loop and thumbs the gate shut; the rocket swings and taps the panel, leaving a red paint smear on the metal ledge. He looks toward the small window. One continuous take. SFX: spring gate snap, tin tapping metal, harness creak. Ambient noise: an off-screen countdown over the speaker, pumps thudding far below, air hissing through vents.

shots.title: the-shaking-starts
shots.firstFrame: Eye-level camera close beside his head, tight medium, 16:9. The man from the reference image fills frame-right in profile, jaw set, eyes forward toward frame-left, pressed back into the seat. The tin rocket hangs on its lanyard in soft foreground frame-left, the red paint smear visible on the ledge behind it. In frame: the man from the reference image pressed into the seat, the harness webbing across his chest, the tin rocket swinging on the lanyard, the paint-smeared panel ledge, cyan dial glow, the small window filled with white light.
shots.motion: Camera shakes with the frame and creeps in a few centimetres as vibration takes the capsule and his face tightens against it. His eyes narrow, one hand grabs the seat edge, loses it, grabs again; his breath comes short and his lips part. The tin rocket rattles hard on the lanyard and a fleck of red paint shakes loose from its nose, leaving bare metal. One continuous take. SFX: deep structural roar, tin rattling on wire, a strained exhale. Ambient noise: an off-screen speaker voice reading altitude, metal groaning, rushing air thinning away.

shots.title: letting-it-go
shots.firstFrame: Low camera height in the dim cupola module, wide size, 16:9. The man from the reference image floats off-center to frame-right, turned frame-left toward the round window, holding the tin rocket loosely between two fingers, its unclipped lanyard drifting free beside him. Blue Earth-light from the window is the only strong source, edging his face and hands. In frame: the man from the reference image floating, the tin rocket in his fingers with a bare metal chip on its nose, the loose lanyard drifting, the round cupola window filled with Earth's blue limb, a handrail in foreground frame-left.
shots.motion: Camera rises slowly from low and holds wide as he opens his fingers and lets the tin rocket go. He hesitates first, thumb pressing the dented nose, then releases; the rocket turns away from him and floats toward the window, and his empty hand stays open in the blue light. He blinks hard, wipes his eye against his shoulder, and grips the handrail to steady himself. One continuous take. SFX: fabric rustle, a soft tin knock against the frame, one unsteady breath. Ambient noise: off-screen fan hum and a faint radio voice from another module.

shots.title: the-whole-world-below
shots.firstFrame: POV through the round cupola window, camera at the man's eye height, wide size, 16:9. The Earth's curved blue limb fills the lower two thirds off-center to frame-left, cloud spirals lit gold along the terminator, black star-scattered space above. The tin rocket drifts in the near foreground frame-right, slowly rotating, the bare metal chip on its nose flashing. In frame: the cupola window frame with one handrail edge, the drifting tin rocket, the Earth's blue limb with cloud spirals and gold terminator, city lights on the night side, stars above the horizon.
shots.motion: Camera holds steady and drifts a few degrees frame-left as the Earth turns beneath the window and the terminator line creeps across the clouds. The tin rocket rotates slowly through the foreground, its bare metal chip catching the blue light once per turn, and taps the window frame, leaving a faint red mark on the glass edge before floating out of frame. One continuous take. SFX: a single soft tin tap on glass. Ambient noise: off-screen fan hum, a faint radio voice reading coordinates, the low pressurised silence of the module.
